atoms.a: What is part of a flower?

feedback.end: Correct. Pollen, petals and seeds are part of many plants and flowers, but there is a lot more. Let’s hear what Tricia the Plant Expert has to say.

atoms.b: Did you know that flowers are not only beautiful to look at, but they are also very ((++complex simple)) living things? Let’s focus on four crucial areas when it comes to their reproduction.
The ((++stamen_is roots_are)) the part of a flower that produces ((++pollen fruits)).
Once the pollen is made, it can be carried by ((++insects leaves)) to pollinate other flowers.
The ((++carpel leaf)) is long, tube-like and often located at the centre of the flower.
The sticky top of the carpel is called the ((++stigma flower)). The pollen sticks to this and travels down the carpel to fertilise the flower’s eggs or ovules.

hint.text: You can scroll up to reread Tricia’s text. She explains what each part of the flower looks like.

b.sound: Pollen is a very fine dust that is necessary for the flower’s reproduction.
Pollen is a tiny insect living inside the flower.

atoms.a: Where can you find pollen in a flower?

b.sound: Pollen is produced inside the stamen of the flower.
Pollen is produced inside the petals of the flower.
